related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of homocystinuria in adults?

text_blocks.snippet: In adults, homocystinuria, an inherited metabolic disorder, can manifest with a range of symptoms, including eye problems like lens dislocation and nearsightedness, skeletal abnormalities like scoliosis and long limbs, and an increased risk of blood clots. Additionally, some adults may experience developmental delays, learning disabilities, and behavioral or psychiatric issues.
snippet_highlighted_words: eye problems like lens dislocation and nearsightedness, skeletal abnormalities like scoliosis and long limbs, and an increased risk of blood clots

text_blocks.snippet: Specific symptoms in adults may include:

list.title: Ophthalmological:
list.snippet: Dislocation of the eye lens (ectopia lentis), severe nearsightedness (myopia).

list.title: Skeletal:
list.snippet: Tall stature, long limbs (arachnodactyly), scoliosis (curvature of the spine), knock knees, chest deformities (pectus excavatum or carinatum).

list.title: Cardiovascular:
list.snippet: Increased risk of blood clots (thromboembolism), potentially leading to stroke or other complications.

list.title: Neurological:
list.snippet: Developmental delays, learning disabilities, behavioral and psychiatric problems, cognitive decline, seizures.

list.title: Other:
list.snippet: Osteoporosis (weakened bones), mental retardation, and in some cases, megaloblastic anemia (a blood disorder).

text_blocks.snippet: Note: While some individuals with homocystinuria may not experience symptoms until adulthood, others may have symptoms that begin in childhood and persist or worsen in later years.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Diagnosis of homocystinuria in adults often involves blood tests to measure homocysteine and other relevant metabolites, as well as genetic testing.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Management typically involves a combination of dietary modifications (low-methionine diet), vitamin supplementation (especially vitamin B6, B12, and folate), and potentially medication like betaine (trimethylglycine), according to Mount Sinai.

list.title: Complications:
list.snippet: Untreated homocystinuria can lead to severe complications, including stroke, blindness, and significant intellectual disability.

text_blocks.snippet: Elevated homocysteine levels, known as hyperhomocysteinemia, typically do not cause specific symptoms. However, in severe cases or when other underlying conditions are present, some symptoms may occur, including:

list.snippet: Cardiovascular problems: Increased risk of heart disease, stroke, and blood clots
Cognitive decline: Memory loss, confusion, and dementia
Bone health problems: Osteoporosis and fractures
Neural tube defects: In newborns with inherited homocystinuria
Skin and hair changes: Pallor, skin rashes, and hair loss
**Numbness and tingling in the hands and feet

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that these symptoms can also be caused by other conditions, so it's essential to consult a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
